source.body:
### Bug Description

Since typeVersion 2, SSE setup and the Streamable HTTP endpoint share one path. A Streamable HTTP client opens its optional server-to-client stream with a GET carrying its `mcp-session-id`. The trigger treats that GET as a new SSE setup: it opens a second, legacy SSE session with a new session ID and sends an `endpoint` event (the Python SDK logs `Unknown SSE event: endpoint`). The stray session stays in the session manager until it is evicted. The spec lets a server that does not offer this stream answer the GET with 405.

### To Reproduce

1. Activate a workflow with an MCP Server Trigger (typeVersion 2).
2. POST an initialize request and read the `mcp-session-id` response header.
3. GET the same path with that header.
4. The response is an SSE stream with `event: endpoint` and a different `sessionId`.

### Expected behavior

405 Method Not Allowed, and no new session.

### Debug Info

```
## core
- n8nVersion: 2.45.5
- platform: docker (self-hosted)
- nodeJsVersion: 26.12.1
- database: sqlite
- executionMode: regular
- license: community
```

### Operating System

Docker (Linux) on Windows 11 / WSL2

### n8n Version

2.45.5

### Node.js Version

26.12.1

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current `master` routing. The GET webhook enters the `setup` branch without checking for an existing `mcp-session-id`, and `handleSetupRequest()` always creates a new SSE transport/session ([McpTrigger.node.ts](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/mcp/McpTrigger/McpTrigger.node.ts#L320-L338), [McpServer.ts](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/mcp/McpTrigger/McpServer.ts#L112-L124)). That matches the stray-session path in the report. A regression test could send GET with an existing Streamable HTTP session header and assert 405 with no additional session registered; the initial GET without that header should continue to establish the legacy SSE connection.
